commitResults.messageTitle: A-MoreOOP: Extract Ui class for all console interaction
commitResults.messageBody:
Move every System.in/System.out touch-point out of Lebron and into a
new Ui class:

- Ui owns the LINE divider and BANNER constants, the Scanner over
  System.in, and the greeting/goodbye blocks.
- Ui exposes readCommand(), showLine(), showMessage(String),
  showWelcome(), showGoodbye() and close().
- Lebron.main() and the parseTaskIndex/parseDeadline/parseEvent helpers
  now take a Ui and route all output through it instead of calling
  System.out directly.

Behaviour is unchanged: the same text is printed in the same order, so
all 26 UI test cases still pass. This is the first step of the
A-MoreOOP refactor (target classes: Ui, Storage, Parser, TaskList);
Storage already exists, so the remaining steps are TaskList and Parser.

commitResults.messageTitle: A-MoreOOP: Extract TaskList class and LebronException
commitResults.messageBody:
Wrap the in-memory ArrayList<Task> in a dedicated TaskList class:

- TaskList offers add(Task), delete(int), mark(int), unmark(int),
  get(int), size() and an unmodifiable asList() view. Task numbers are
  1-based and TaskList does the range checking in one place.
- New LebronException carries a ready-to-show message; TaskList throws
  it for an out-of-range task number instead of the caller pre-checking
  against tasks.size().
- parseTaskIndex() drops its range check (and the taskCount parameter);
  it now only reports a missing / non-numeric argument. The command
  switch in Lebron.main() is wrapped in try/catch(LebronException) so an
  out-of-range number is reported the same way as before.
- Storage.save() now takes a TaskList (iterating asList()) rather than a
  raw List<Task>.

Behaviour is unchanged; all 26 UI test cases still pass. Remaining
A-MoreOOP step: extract Parser (the Command enum and the
parse* helpers).

commitResults.messageTitle: A-MoreOOP: Extract Parser and simplify the run loop
commitResults.messageBody:
Move all command interpretation out of Lebron into a Parser class:

- Parser.parse(String) returns a ParsedCommand value object (a type
  plus the typed data that command needs: a description, a pre-built
  Task, or a 1-based task number). Unknown keywords, missing
  descriptions, non-numeric task numbers and unparseable dates are now
  reported by throwing LebronException instead of printing via Ui and
  returning null.
- The Command enum and the parseTaskIndex / parseDeadline / parseEvent
  helpers moved from Lebron to Parser (helpers now throw instead of
  printing).
- Lebron.main() is now a small read-parse-run loop: read a line, show
  the divider, Parser.parse(), runCommand(), show the divider, repeat
  until the command signals exit. A single catch(LebronException) turns
  every input/execution error into a shown message, so all errors are
  handled uniformly.
- "bye" now flows through the same loop (its handler prints the
  farewell) rather than being special-cased before the divider; the
  emitted text is identical.

Behaviour unchanged; all 26 UI test cases still pass. This completes the
A-MoreOOP minimal target (Ui, Storage, Parser, TaskList all extracted).

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Javadoc header comments to all non-private members
Reformat code to follow the SE-EDU Java conding standard
Add find command to search tasks by keyword
A-CheckStyle: add Checkstyle with the AB3 rule set
Bundle JavaFX into the shadow jar
Use assertions to document key invariants
commitResults.messageBody:
Add five Java assert statements (not JUnit) at points where later code
assumes an earlier check already held: a non-blank task description,
Task.fromFileFormat's switch always assigning task, TaskList.get's
range check, Lebron.execute's unreachable default case, and
MainWindow's Main-wires-lebron-first contract. Each keeps its existing
exception/behaviour intact for a plain (non -ea) run; the assert only
adds a fail-fast check under -ea. 97 JUnit tests (run with assertions
enabled by Gradle) and 29 UI tests still pass.

Level 10's refactor moved the farewell text into Lebron.execute()'s
BYE case, printed like any other response. showGoodbye() has had no
call sites since, and dead code is only baggage -- version control
already preserves it if ever needed again.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace magic numbers in Main with named constants
commitResults.messageBody:
400/600/340/220 for the window's default and minimum size gave no hint
what they meant at the call site. Named as DEFAULT_WIDTH/HEIGHT and
MIN_WIDTH/HEIGHT.

commitResults.messageTitle: Polish Task: rename doneBit(), drop a redundant comment
commitResults.messageBody:
- Methods should read as verbs (actions), not nouns -- doneBit() read
  as a thing, not an action. Renamed to getDoneBit(), matching the
  getX() convention already used elsewhere in this class; updated its
  three call sites in Todo/Deadline/Event.
- Removed the trailing '// mark done task with X' on getStatusIcon(),
  which restated exactly what the Javadoc directly above it already
  says.

commitResults.messageTitle: Break Lebron.execute() into one handler per command
commitResults.messageBody:
execute()'s switch was 50 lines and mixed two abstraction levels in
every branch: deciding what to do, and how to do it (violates SLAP).
Its LIST and FIND cases also duplicated the same 'header + numbered
list' logic almost verbatim.

Extract one handleX() method per command, plus a shared
formatTaskList(header, tasks) helper for LIST/FIND. execute() is now
a 23-line pure dispatcher; the duplication is gone. Behaviour is
unchanged -- 97 JUnit tests and 29 UI tests still pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use Streams for TaskList.find and Storage.save
commitResults.messageBody:
Both were plain filter/map loops over a collection -- find() kept
matching tasks, save() transformed each task to its file-format
string. Rewrote as tasks.stream().filter(...).collect(...) and
.stream().map(Task::toFileFormat).collect(...), which read as what
each does rather than how. Left Lebron's numbered-list builder and
Storage.load's per-line try/catch as loops -- neither composes
cleanly with Streams (indexed output; per-element exception handling
with a failure count) without hurting readability.

97 JUnit tests and 29 UI tests still pass.
Use assertions to document key invariants
Use Streams for TaskList.find and Storage.save

Add /every day|week|month to deadline/event so they repeat. Marking a
recurring task done rolls its date(s) forward to the next occurrence
instead of staying marked done (Deadline/Event override markAsDone());
Event advances both endpoints together to preserve its duration.

The recurrence period is an optional trailing field in the data file
(5th for D, 6th for E) so existing save files without one still load
unchanged. An unrecognised period is rejected at the command line and
treated as corruption (skip + warn) if found in the data file.

Implemented per the reviewed specification (product decisions:
Deadline/Event only, /every flag on the existing commands, roll-
forward-in-place on mark, fixed day/week/month presets). 136 JUnit
tests and 35 UI test cases pass; 0 Checkstyle violations.
